transcript:
00:00 Ava: hi everyone thanks for joining, we have about 40 minutes, is this time still good?
00:04 Lena: yeah this works for us, thanks Ava. quick context, we've got renewal coming up end of April and our usage has grown about 2.6x since last quarter so we wanted to talk capacity and regions.
00:12 Ava: perfect, that's exactly what we planned to cover. Samir from our infra team is here for the technical bits.
00:18 Samir: hey all, morning. I'll jump in on the benchmarks and networking stuff.
00:25 Marcus: to set expectation, our peak is moving from 2k to around 6k rps for gen endpoints and embeddings are up too; we're seeing some 95th and 99th spike on tail latency, particularly during batch jobs.
00:34 Priya: also want to surface that compliance has a tight window for review so if we can get SOC2 and KMS docs soon that helps.
00:42 Ava: got it. high level, there are three levers here: increase Dedicated pool size (more GPUs), add an EU region to reduce cross-region latency for EU customers, or optimize batching/quantization which Samir can help recommend.
01:05 Samir: on batching and q bits, we've seen about 20-30% cost reduction without hurt to p50 latency for similar workloads, but p99 needs careful config. For Prism's token distribution you sent, we should run a focused bench.
01:20 Marcus: yeah we'll share a token histogram, it's in the drive - link in chat.
01:28 Ava: great. on Dedicated sizing, currently you're on an 8x reserved pool. Two options we discussed in the pre-read: 16x reserved or keep 8x but add burst capacity and EU region. The 16x gives predictable throughput and better tail latency under sustained load.
01:46 Lena: what's the rough delta on price and how does a 12 vs 24 month commitment change numbers?
01:52 Ava: I'll send the spreadsheet with both terms, but ballpark — 12-mo on 16x is about 1.9x the 8x monthly spend; 24-mo we can extend about 12% discount on top. Exact numbers in sheet.
02:06 Marcus: one question — if we move to 16x in US-only today and add EU later, does the pool split or do we need separate dedicated pools per region?
02:14 Samir: you need region-specific pools for capacity locality; we can route traffic by policy (latency-first) and the control plane supports fallback to other region if local pool is saturated. There's a short config on routing tables we'll share.
02:30 Priya: how does data residency work with logs and KV cache? We need EU data not leaving region for certain customers.
02:36 Samir: we support per-region KV cache and prefix caching. For Private/VPC deployments we can lock storage to region; for Hosted/Dedicated we have region tenancy and log retention options. I'll point to the doc where we had the EU residency notes.
02:53 Lena: can you confirm compliance: SOC2 type II, SSO SAML, audit logs, and KMS?
02:58 Ava: yes, we are SOC2 Type II; we support SAML SSO and have audit logs. For KMS we integrate with customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK). I'll attach the security pack.
03:12 Priya: would you share the exact SOC2 report or a redacted copy? Legal needs that to clear renewal.
03:18 Ava: absolutely, we'll send the redacted SOC2 and SOC bridge doc; expect that in the next 48 hours.
03:24 Marcus: on performance — can you run a 10k qps synthetic bench with our token distribution and measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens?
03:32 Samir: yes, we can do that on a dedicated bench. We'll probably need the sample traffic and you to allow a short test window on your account or share artifacts.
03:40 Marcus: we can provide the traces and a small service account. We'll do that after this call.
03:46 Ava: perfect. any blockers for doing 16x?
03:49 Lena: main blocker is budget sign-off; also want to understand failure modes and how graceful degradation works when the pool is saturated.
03:58 Samir: on graceful degradation we have automatic fallback policies — route to a lower-cost model variant or to hosted pool; we can set hard limits and throttles. There is an outage playbook for Dedicated. I'll share it.
04:12 Lena: and SLA?
04:14 Ava: Dedicated comes with SLA commitments on uptime and latency tiers; exact numbers depend on the pool and region. We'll include SLA terms in the commercial deck.
04:22 Marcus: curious about quantization recommendations — we tried int8 earlier and saw some quality drift on classification tasks.
04:29 Samir: yeah quantization tradeoffs depend on model and eval set. Redwood's Optimize engine recommends profiles per workload; for classification you might need q4_0 or q8 with calibration. We'll run an eval on your eval set.
04:46 Priya: one more compliance question: do you provide per-token retention settings and the ability to disable logs for certain routes?
04:52 Ava: yes, route-level retention and scrub rules supported; you can also opt-out for PII-sensitive routes. We'll include the runbook.
05:00 Lena: timeline-wise, if we want to lock pricing and start 16x by May 1, what's the signing timeline?
05:07 Ava: for May 1 start, we recommend signing by the third week of April to provision capacity and run warm-up benches. Legal review typically 7-14 days if no custom amendments.
05:18 Marcus: for EU region, what's lead time?
05:20 Samir: adding an EU region for Dedicated is about 3-4 weeks to provision and validate routing, shorter if we parallelize provisioning with the US pool setup.
05:32 Priya: are there any one-off migration costs to mirror KV cache or do we cold-start in EU?
05:36 Samir: cold-starting cache in EU is typical; we can do proactive warm-up via traffic mirroring or batch prepopulation to avoid tail spikes. There might be minimal one-time data transfer charges depending on where you seed from. We'll estimate that.
05:51 Ava: quick note — competitors came up in pre-sales. Prism evaluated Anthropic and built some in-house infra. We positioned Redwood on predictable economics and easier rollouts.
06:02 Lena: one internal objection was around vendor lock-in — can you describe exportability of configs and models?
06:08 Samir: configs are exportable as YAML, and model versions can be pinned and we support container-based private deployments if you want a self-managed path later.
06:20 Marcus: ok. next steps recap?
06:23 Ava: I'll go first: 1) send updated commercial spreadsheet for 16x 12/24 mo options + EU add-on link (Ava, by 2026-03-24); 2) attach SOC2 and security pack (Ava, within 48 hours); 3) Samir to run targeted bench with Prism token distribution and produce p50/p95/p99 and cost metrics (Samir, by 2026-03-26); 4) Prism to share traffic histogram and grant service account for bench (Marcus, by 2026-03-25); 5) schedule technical deep-dive on VPC/KMS integration wk of 2026-03-29 (Ava to coordinate).
06:58 Lena: that sounds good. any last questions?
07:02 Priya: just please include the audit contact for SOC queries.
07:05 Ava: will do. thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the deck and links.
07:10 Marcus: thanks all.
07:12 Samir: thanks.
07:15 Lena: bye.
42:00 [call ended]

Notes: transcription contains typical automated errors — product names occasionally mis-typed (Redwod). Shared artifacts: pricing spreadsheet (https://redwood.example.com/quotes/PRISM-5821), security pack link (internal), bench artifacts to follow in GDrive.
